newsitem.title: UK: Moody's sees good fundamentals at Spanish banks.
newsitem.headline: Moody's sees good fundamentals at Spanish banks.

text.p: Moodys Investors Service said in a report on the Spanish banking system on Tuesday that Spain's banks appear to be preserving their generally sound fundamentals, although smaller banks may come under pressure.
Moody's said this might result in wider ratings variations over the next several years.

"Such distinctions will reflect the degree to which individual banks successfully adopt to a more competitive banking environment both in their domestic market and in their overseas markets," said Maria Cabanyes Trevino, senior analyst at Moody's and author of the report.
Moody's said Spain's major banks enjoy strong capitalisation, prudent loan provisioning, and acceptable net interest margins -- all factors that sustain their present ratings.

But the banks' earning capacities were "hampered by a cumbersome, expensive cost structure, a low interest rate environment, strong domestic competition and also by only modest diversification of revenue streams".

Moody's added the situation would push the Spanish banks to more aggressively pursue foreign franchises -- particularly in Latin America -- and would also perhaps tempt their managements to compromise underwriting standards, to price with less caution, and to enter traditionally riskier activities.

Moody's said it currently rates nine banking groups in Spain. "The average senior debt rating is Aa3, the average rating of the banks for their long-term deposits is Aa3, and the average financial strength rating for this universe is B."

Given an intensely competitive environment, and spurred by more demanding shareholders seeking richer returns, Spanish banks would have to exert themselves to bolster revenues without incurring greater risks, Moody's said.
"The ability to set tight underwriting standards and keep pricing correct in relation to the risks assumed to hold on to market share will be a key challenge," said Cabanyes.
Another challenge is the Spanish banks' ability to follow an international strategy without taking undue business and balance sheet chances, Moody's said.
"In this context, certain highly rated banks are embarking on an aggressive Latin American expansion." Moody's said this may lead to rating adjustments to factor in this potential source of risk.

Cabanyes said pressures on traditional earnings were not unique to Spanish banks, but that institutions still enjoyed a few fundamental strengths that should place them in a good position when compared with their European peers.
